lessons.title: Share our made up story
lessons.outcome: Perform our drama (World Book Day link).
lessons.goal: I can share my part in our made-up story.
success: I can use a start and end cue.
I can share or direct my real part.
I can log what I did and who saw it.
words: A sign to start or stop.
The people who watch or listen.

artist_cards.work: The new den with hand pictures
artist_cards.description: First the group point to a big space. Next they show that the space is small. Last they make a small roof with their hands. A hand cue helps them hold each picture for three counts.
artist_cards.notice: What comes first? What comes last?
artist_cards.prompt: Which cue could help us share our story?
artist_cards.model_answer: The big space comes first. The small roof comes last. A small hand cue could help the group change picture together.

artist_cards.work: The new den with short lines
artist_cards.description: One voice says, We want a den. Next a voice says, The space is small. Last a voice says, We can make a small den. Each person stays in their own space.
artist_cards.notice: Which line tells us the change?
artist_cards.prompt: Would you use a voice, a hand cue or both? Why?
artist_cards.model_answer: The space is small tells us the change. Any clear, safe choice of voice or silent cue is valid if the pupil gives a reason.

staff_guidance.plain_language: Resilience can include pausing, asking for help, changing a plan and trying again. Do not ask pupils to recreate personal change, hide feelings or work through pain.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. GROW retains an optional Bronze-stretch layer, labelled Optional next level stretch on pupil tasks. Retain only actual evidence. These lessons and a completed checklist do not automatically complete the award. Review the complete real portfolio and record any gaps with a next action.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: The original den or smaller-show-space stories can be told with three still hand pictures, short lines or quiet original sound. A clear small example is enough. Judge each pupil's own choice and contribution, not confidence, acting style or length of performance. Do not use accents, real people or disability as a character trait.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Agree the open-hand stop signal, clear personal spaces and quiet return route. Pupils may perform seated, speak, sign, use small silent moves or direct an adult. A private share with one member of the class or invited staff is valid. Offer a pass on the group audience. No personal disclosure, contact, running, sudden sound, darkness, costumes or forced facial expressions.
staff_guidance.safety: All props and story spaces are imagined. Keep movement within each person's own clear space; no den building, objects to climb on, stage combat, lifting, touching, blindfolds or breath holding. Hold a comfortable pose for about three seconds, breathe normally, then relax. Keep exits clear. Quiet sound stays at talking level or below. Record directed work as direction; do not claim the pupil physically or vocally performed an adult's action.
staff_guidance.audience: Only members of the class and invited staff may form the audience. There are no outside guests, public audience, families or external invitations. Confirm who is actually present. A private share may use one class member or invited staff member. Record an audience only when the share has really occurred.
prompt_ladder: Point to the instruction or place.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Use one cue at a time. Rehearse the three or four story parts with a short model. Give two concrete choices, then fade the prompt. For reflection, sort one real item at a time under A, B, C or D; leave an honest gap if evidence is missing.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Allow pointing, signing, a sketch, speech or an adult scribe. Give processing time. Read dictated words back and let the pupil correct them. Do not assess eye contact, accent or facial expression. Use I chose ... because ... and Next I will ... .
adaptations.semh: Keep all stories invented and low stakes. Let the pupil choose a role and amount of sharing. A pause or request for help can be a planned choice in the story. Agree a calm return cue. Review evidence without ranking pupils or comparing attendance.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Offer seated hand poses and a silent directing role. Keep clear personal spaces. No pupil is moved into a pose. Offer a quiet private audience within the class or invited staff. An observation note can replace a photo or recording.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Model first, next, last and change with gestures. Let pupils use their own language to explain a choice before adding a short English label. Check meaning before writing a confirmed arts-log note.

misconceptions.claim: A group performance is evidence of every pupil's contribution.
misconceptions.correction: Record each pupil's real role, choices, action or direction, support and confirmed words separately.

misconceptions.claim: A planned audience or teacher example can fill a missing record.
misconceptions.correction: Record only actual events and work. Mark a missing item pending and add a specific next action; never invent attendance, audience or feedback.

misconceptions.claim: Completing today's arts log means the award is complete.
misconceptions.correction: The log gathers evidence. The complete real portfolio needs a separate review against the award requirements.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Performers and production teams use cues, respect an audience, review real feedback and keep clear records of their own work.
staff_guidance.book_link: The exact source outcome retains its book-day wording as a thematic story and book connection. This performance is scheduled for Monday 22 March 2027. Do not describe that date as World Book Day. Use only the original invented den story or a pupil's new invented story; no published characters, copied text or costumes are needed.

lessons.artist_use_note: These are invented classroom performance examples. They are not records of real artists, an external arts visit or pupil work. Use them to compare a technique, then retain each pupil's own actual choice and view.

ta_focus.I do: Point to one clear cue or one real evidence item. Separate the teacher model from the pupil's own work.
ta_focus.We do: Ask each pupil to make or confirm a choice. If the hinge answer is uncertain, model one concrete contrast or evidence check before returning the decision.
ta_focus.Independent: Use the prompt ladder. Record actual help. Return the next choice to the pupil, and retain their own confirmed words.

lessons.evidence: Retain a dated note of each pupil's real role, choices and work or direction, actual audience when sharing occurred, real feedback if given, and support used. Keep an honest gap for anything not done. A photo or recording is optional and follows local consent procedures. A group product never replaces the individual contribution record.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Our story is made up.
Pick act, speak, sign or direct.
Our audience is our class and invited staff only.
stages.say: Today is our first lesson of the week and our chance to share a short story. A book can tell a story; we tell ours with moves and short lines. Choose a role or a quiet directing job. Agree the stop signal and who from the class or invited staff is actually here. There are no outside guests.
stages.good: Each pupil chooses or confirms a role and audience route. The invented story, space and stop signal are clear.
stages.fallback: Offer one seated hand move or let the pupil direct the adult. A private share with one class member or invited staff member is available.
stages.answer: A short silent part or a directed part is valid. Record what the pupil actually chooses; do not treat a pass as a performance.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Find our real story plan.
Show first, next and last.
Try the start cue once.
stages.say: Use the genuine plan and choices made earlier. Our den story can be: first we want a den, next the space is small, last we choose a small den. If work is missing or the pupil was away, make that fresh three-part plan now and date it today. Do not claim a previous rehearsal.
stages.good: Pupils recall a real sequence or make a fresh dated one. The start cue is practised calmly.
stages.fallback: Point wide, bring hands close, then make a small roof shape. The pupil may cue the adult for each part.
stages.answer: First is the wish for a den; next is the small space; last is the new small-den plan. A different original three-part story is valid if the order is clear.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch the two class examples.
See a clear start.
See the change and the end.
Which cue helps us?
stages.say: Demonstrate the two invented den examples. I use a hand cue, hold each comfortable pose for three counts and relax. I keep my own space and breathe normally. Check after the model: which part shows the space changed? Explain that the teacher model is not the pupil's evidence.
stages.good: Adult demonstrates a complete safe tiny story and an explicit check. Pupils identify the middle small-space part.
stages.fallback: Use seated hand shapes. Ask the pupil to choose wide or close hands for the middle part; adult follows their direction.
stages.answer: Close hands show the space is small in this model. The final roof shape shows the response. Meaning should be confirmed by the maker.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Agree first, next and last.
Give each person a real part.
Try a start and end cue.
Keep our own space.
stages.say: Choose roles such as mover, voice or cue keeper. Try one calm rehearsal. Hinge: if a pupil wants a quiet share, should we force a class show or offer one class member or invited staff member? Choose the quiet share. If unclear, model the private route and ask again. Confirm the actual audience before the share.
stages.good: Every pupil has an agreed access route and real contribution. Pupils understand that a private share within the allowed audience is valid.
stages.fallback: Adult performs under pupil direction. Use a small hand cue and let the pupil choose one listener from the class or invited staff.
stages.answer: Offer the private share. Never force public acting or add outside guests. If the pupil passes entirely, record the real choice and a next action, not a completed performance.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Share our short story.
Use your chosen role and cue.
You may share with just one class member or invited staff member.
A watcher says: I notice ___.
Keep a note of your real part.
stages.say: This is the performance slot. Groups share in turn to the class and any invited staff who are actually present. Each pupil may share a short section privately within that audience or direct an adult. Use the den sequence or a short original story. Before starting, confirm the cue and chosen part. A watcher names one feature they really saw or heard. Record the real date, audience, individual contribution and help; if no share occurs, mark it pending and name the next action.
stages.good: A real performance or private directed share occurs with the allowed audience, or an honest pending record is kept. Each pupil's own part is identified separately from the group story.
stages.fallback: Pupil directs a seated adult to show three hand pictures to one class member or invited staff member. Record direction and the real listener; no device is required.
stages.answer: Example only: I gave the start cue. One class member watched our three pictures and noticed the pause. Only record that if it happened. Do not copy this teacher model into a pupil log.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Say what you really shared.
Who watched or listened?
What did they really notice?
Store your plan and note.
stages.say: Ask each maker about one real contribution and one actual watcher notice. If no feedback was given, write no feedback yet and choose a later action. Use the final two minutes to clear the space and store the plan and actual note for tomorrow's review.
stages.good: The pupil confirms actual audience and contribution; no invented praise, feedback or attendance is added. Records are stored.
stages.fallback: Use a point or sign to confirm the role and listener. Adult reads a short witnessed note back and lets the pupil correct it.
stages.answer: A useful observation is: I noticed the end pose. A pupil who directed the end cue is recorded as director. Missing feedback stays missing until it is received.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: I shared / directed ___.
My audience was ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
Keep my real work for tomorrow.
stages.say: Keep a dated log of the real share or a pending note. I can write your exact words and read them back. Tomorrow we will review our skills and sort our real arts-log evidence. No checklist will turn a missed share into a completed one.
stages.good: A dated entry distinguishes actual work, directed work and pending work. The pupil confirms a choice and reason.
stages.fallback: Pupil points to the actual role and confirms a short adult note. If the share was not completed, record one practical next action.
stages.answer: Example only: I directed the small-roof pose to show the new plan. My audience was one invited staff member. Record only today's actual work.

Supported: Pick a role or direct the adult.
Use first, next and last hand pictures.
Share with one class member or invited staff member.
Tell or show your real part.
Independent: Use our real three-part story plan.
Share your part with clear start and end cues.
Ask one watcher what they noticed.
Log what you did, who watched and your choice.
Aspire: Make the change and new plan clear.
Use a calm cue to help the group.
Explain one choice and keep real feedback.

log: Today I performed / directed / chose to pass ___.
My real part was ___.
My audience was ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
The watcher noticed ___ / no feedback yet.
Help I used was ___.
If pending, my next action is ___.
misconceptions: The book link needs a real story character
Use our own invented story. A book and a scene can both tell a story.
I must act for everyone
You may share privately with one class member or invited staff member, or direct an adult.
Our group share proves what I did
Keep a real note of your own role and choices.
kit: For three or four pupils: books or arts logs and pencils.
Real prior story plans if available; fresh three-part den cue if missing.
Clear personal spaces or safe seats; all den props are imagined.
Audience limited to the class and invited staff actually present. No external invitations or guests.
No camera, costume, copied book text or device is needed. Keep actual share notes for Tuesday.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Point wide. Say: We want a den. Give a calm start cue.
15 to 30 seconds
Bring hands close. Say: The space is small. Hold for three comfortable counts.
30 to 45 seconds
Make a small roof with hands. Say: We can make a small den.
45 to 60 seconds
Give an end cue and relax. Ask a real watcher to name one feature.
models: Teacher model only: I gave the cue for the last picture. One class member watched and noticed our still end.
Teacher model only: I chose to pass today. My share is pending. Next I will choose a quiet listener from class or invited staff.
lessons.cover: Use the original three-part den story and real prior plans. Practise start and end cues, then give the Create stage to the actual performance or private share. Audience is only the class and invited staff. A pupil may direct a seated adult. Record the real role, listener and any actual feedback. Missing work starts fresh today; an uncompleted share stays pending. Retain records for Tuesday's review.

cold_call.middle: Which cue helps the story end?
cold_call.higher: How did your choice help a watcher follow the change?

lessons.title: Review my drama and arts log
lessons.outcome: Reflect on my drama skills; arts-log evidence.
lessons.goal: I can say what I did and sort my real arts-log work.
success: I can name one drama skill I used.
I can show my own work and choice.
I can mark a gap and a next step.
words: Something you can get better at.
Look back at what you did.
Real work or a note of what happened.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your real plan and share note.
You can point, speak, sign or draw.
A gap is okay. We will plan a next step.
stages.say: Today is our review and arts-log closing lesson. Find yesterday's actual plan and share note if they exist. If you were away or did not share, we record that honestly. You do not need to act a missed performance or invent a watcher to fill a box.
stages.good: Pupils access genuine records without pressure. Missing work is identified calmly and the purpose of the lesson is review.
stages.fallback: Read one real item aloud or use a witnessed note. If there is no earlier item, start a fresh review page dated today and mark the missing evidence pending.
stages.answer: A review can be complete and honest even when some evidence is pending. A gap needs a next action, not invented work.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Point to a skill: cue, pose or voice.
Which one did you really use or direct?
Show the real note if you have it.
stages.say: Name cue, pose and voice. Ask the pupil which was part of their actual work or direction. A pupil may say not yet. If the record is unclear, ask for their own account and label it as pupil recollection rather than a witnessed event.
stages.good: Pupils distinguish a skill actually used from a future goal and connect it to a real item where available.
stages.fallback: Offer two skill words and ask for a point. Adult reads the prior note and asks whether it is right.
stages.answer: A cue helps a start, turn or stop; a pose is a brief still picture; voice can include pace and pause. Record direction as direction.

stages.name: I do
pupil: See a teacher review example.
A real note shows what happened.
A blank space means not yet.
What would we do next?
stages.say: Model with clearly labelled teacher examples: "I gave the end cue; the real note shows my role" and "There was no feedback; I will ask a class member next time." Put the first under real work and the second under next step. Check: can I write that an audience clapped if no one recorded or remembers it happening?
stages.good: Adult models evidence and gap handling without pretending to hold pupil evidence. Pupils reject an unsupported event claim.
stages.fallback: Show a real blank line and say not yet. Offer a choice: make it up or ask for a real next chance.
stages.answer: No. Keep the honest gap and plan a real next action. A teacher example belongs to the teacher model, not the pupil's arts log.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Sort one real class example.
A: take part. B: explore.
C: create. D: share.
What is real? What is pending?
stages.say: Use one actual class item without naming a pupil, or a labelled teacher model. A is a part done; B is an example explored and own view; C is an idea and a real trial; D is a real share. Hinge: a plan says "share tomorrow" but there is no share note. Is D complete? If unsure, compare a plan with a witnessed share note and decide again.
stages.good: Pupils recognise the four arts-log headings and distinguish a planned share from actual sharing. A single item may support more than one area if its real content does.
stages.fallback: Read one heading at a time and offer one real item or pending choice. Adult holds items while the pupil directs the sort.
stages.answer: D is pending until the share really happens. A plan can support C, but it does not prove a share or audience. Do not add invented dates or feedback.

stages.name: Create
pupil: In your arts log, review your real work.
A: what did I do? B: what did I notice?
C: what did I make or change? D: what did I share?
Name one skill and one choice.
Mark any gap: pending. Add a next step.
stages.say: This slot is for reflection and closing the arts log. Work through A, B, C and D using each pupil's actual items. A: real part and help. B: real example, source and own notice or view. C: own idea, trial and chosen change. D: actual share, date, allowed audience and any real feedback. Label invented class examples honestly. Add a short skill review, choice and reason. For each gap write pending, the exact item needed and next action, such as ask an invited staff listener for a quiet share at the next agreed lesson. Do not manufacture a missed performance today in the record.
stages.good: A genuine closing evidence list identifies available items and honest gaps across A to D. Pupil adds a specific skill reflection and next step. Staff record actual help and read scribed words back.
stages.fallback: Adult reads one real item at a time. Pupil points to keep or pending and confirms a short choice sentence. A sketch or gesture can be the reflection.
stages.answer: Example only: A has my cue note. B has my view of the class example. C has my three-part plan. D is pending because I did not share. Next I will ask for a quiet share with invited staff. This is a model, not evidence to copy.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Check the list with an adult.
Does it show my own work?
Are dates and audience real?
Keep the real items together.
stages.say: Read the evidence list and pupil words back. Ask which part they want to correct. Check an item location for each available entry and a next action for each gap. A completed list is not a decision that the award is finished. Reserve the final two minutes for calm storage.
stages.good: Pupil confirms the record; real items are findable and gaps are visible. No automatic award completion claim is made.
stages.fallback: Adult checks one entry at a time and accepts yes, no or a correction by point or sign.
stages.answer: An honest list may include several pending items. Keep the pupil's own confirmed view and do not replace it with polished adult wording.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: My skill was ___.
My choice was ___ because ___.
My next step is ___.
My arts log shows my real work.
stages.say: Complete a final short reflection or witnessed note. Say what is ready to review and what remains pending. Store the real evidence together. Completing this lesson or checklist does not automatically complete the award.
stages.good: A dated personal reflection, evidence locations and next action close the lesson. Award completion is not asserted.
stages.fallback: Pupil confirms one skill and one next step. Adult writes exactly what was confirmed and records support.
stages.answer: Example only: I used a hand cue. I kept it because our end was clear. Next I will wait until each person is ready. Use the pupil's own actual reflection.

Supported: Look at one real item with an adult.
Point: did it happen or is it pending?
Sort under A, B, C or D with help.
Say or show one skill and a next step.
Independent: Sort your real work under A, B, C and D.
Name your part, choice and a reason.
Check dates, audience and help used.
Mark each gap pending and add a next action.
Aspire: Complete the same real evidence list.
Use two real items to show a skill change.
Explain which choice helped your story.
Choose a small next skill goal and how to check it.

log: My real drama role or direction was ___.
One skill I used was ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
A Take part: my real item is ___ / pending.
B Explore: my real example and own view are ___ / pending.
C Create: my idea, trial and change are ___ / pending.
D Share: my real share date and audience are ___ / pending.
Real feedback was ___ / no feedback yet.
My gap and next action are ___.
Help I used was ___.
misconceptions: A gap means I must fill it with a model
Keep pending and add one real next action. A model is not pupil work.
A photo proves all my choices
Keep your own words and role note as well. A photo is optional.
A full list means I have finished the award
The full real portfolio still needs a separate review.
kit: For three or four pupils: books or arts logs, pencils and each pupil's real plans, trials and share notes.
A, B, C and D log headings; adult can read them aloud.
Space to keep each pupil's actual items together without mixing group and individual evidence.
No new public performance, outside visitor, device or photograph is needed.
If an item is missing, record pending, the item needed and the next action.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Point to a teacher model of a real role note. Say: This tells what I did.
15 to 30 seconds
Point to a blank share record. Say: I do not know that a share happened. It is pending.
30 to 45 seconds
Sort the real note under A. Keep a planned share separate from D.
45 to 60 seconds
Say: My next action is to ask for a quiet share with a class member or invited staff.
models: Teacher model only: I used a calm end cue. My real role note is under A, and my plan is under C.
Teacher model only: D is pending because I did not share. Next I will arrange a quiet share with an invited staff member.
lessons.cover: This is the second-slot review and arts-log closing lesson. Use actual plans, trials and Monday share notes. Teach A Take part, B Explore, C Create and D Share; sort real items and record the pupil's own skill reflection. Missing work or feedback is pending with a specific next action. Do not invent a performance, audience or attendance, and do not declare the award complete.

cold_call.foundation: Which real item shows your part?
cold_call.middle: Which skill did you use or direct, and why?
cold_call.higher: What is still pending and what exact action will help?

closing_evidence_list: A Take part: keep a real dated note of what you did or directed and the help you used.
B Explore: keep a real example you saw or heard, its source, what you noticed and your own view. Label an invented class model as a class model.
C Create: keep your own idea, a real trial or outline, a change you tested and your reason.
D Share: keep what you really shared, the actual date and audience, and any feedback that really happened. If no feedback was given, say so.
For any gap: mark pending, name the missing item and agree the next action.
Keep the pupil's own confirmed skill reflection, choice, reason and actual support. The complete real portfolio requires a separate award review.

lessons.title: Perform our story about a new plan
lessons.goal: I can share my own part in a short performance for our allowed audience.
success: I can use my agreed role and cues.
I can perform or direct for a real class or invited staff audience.
I can record my own part and real feedback.
words: The people who watch or listen.
A sign for a start, pause or end.
Your own part in shared work.
A useful notice about what happened.

artist_cards.work: A smaller show space with words
artist_cards.description: The group plan wide moves. The imagined space gets smaller. A planner asks for ideas. The group test small hand moves, choose one and end together. A narrator uses short lines to mark the change and the new plan.
artist_cards.notice: What makes the change and response clear?
artist_cards.prompt: How could a short line or pause help our audience?
artist_cards.model_answer: The wide-to-small moves show the change; asking for ideas and choosing a small move show the response. A short line or pause can give an audience time to follow the new plan.

artist_cards.work: A smaller show space in silence
artist_cards.description: The group begin with wide hand poses. A point to the word Change marks a smaller space. Each offers a small move. They choose one and repeat it together, then hold a final pose. The intended meaning is explained after the share.
artist_cards.notice: How does the group show a choice without speech?
artist_cards.prompt: Which feature would you keep in your own piece, and why?
artist_cards.model_answer: Offering moves and then repeating one together shows a choice. A pupil might keep the clear point, repeat or final pose for a reason linked to their own intention.

staff_guidance.plain_language: Resilience can include pausing, asking for help, changing a plan and trying again. Do not ask pupils to recreate personal change, hide feelings or work through pain.
staff_guidance.scope: Both pathways work at Explore. GROW retains an optional Bronze-stretch layer, labelled Optional next level stretch on pupil tasks. Retain only actual evidence. These lessons and a completed checklist do not automatically complete the award. Review the complete real portfolio and record any gaps with a next action.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: The original den or smaller-show-space stories can be told with three still hand pictures, short lines or quiet original sound. A clear small example is enough. Judge each pupil's own choice and contribution, not confidence, acting style or length of performance. Do not use accents, real people or disability as a character trait.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Agree the open-hand stop signal, clear personal spaces and quiet return route. Pupils may perform seated, speak, sign, use small silent moves or direct an adult. A private share with one member of the class or invited staff is valid. Offer a pass on the group audience. No personal disclosure, contact, running, sudden sound, darkness, costumes or forced facial expressions.
staff_guidance.safety: All props and story spaces are imagined. Keep movement within each person's own clear space; no den building, objects to climb on, stage combat, lifting, touching, blindfolds or breath holding. Hold a comfortable pose for about three seconds, breathe normally, then relax. Keep exits clear. Quiet sound stays at talking level or below. Record directed work as direction; do not claim the pupil physically or vocally performed an adult's action.
staff_guidance.audience: Only members of the class and invited staff may form the audience. There are no outside guests, public audience, families or external invitations. Confirm who is actually present. A private share may use one class member or invited staff member. Record an audience only when the share has really occurred.
prompt_ladder: Point to the instruction or place.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Use one cue at a time. Rehearse the three or four story parts with a short model. Give two concrete choices, then fade the prompt. For reflection, sort one real item at a time under A, B, C or D; leave an honest gap if evidence is missing.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Allow pointing, signing, a sketch, speech or an adult scribe. Give processing time. Read dictated words back and let the pupil correct them. Do not assess eye contact, accent or facial expression. Use I chose ... because ... and Next I will ... .
adaptations.semh: Keep all stories invented and low stakes. Let the pupil choose a role and amount of sharing. A pause or request for help can be a planned choice in the story. Agree a calm return cue. Review evidence without ranking pupils or comparing attendance.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Offer seated hand poses and a silent directing role. Keep clear personal spaces. No pupil is moved into a pose. Offer a quiet private audience within the class or invited staff. An observation note can replace a photo or recording.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Model first, next, last and change with gestures. Let pupils use their own language to explain a choice before adding a short English label. Check meaning before writing a confirmed arts-log note.

misconceptions.claim: A group performance is evidence of every pupil's contribution.
misconceptions.correction: Record each pupil's real role, choices, action or direction, support and confirmed words separately.

misconceptions.claim: A planned audience or teacher example can fill a missing record.
misconceptions.correction: Record only actual events and work. Mark a missing item pending and add a specific next action; never invent attendance, audience or feedback.

misconceptions.claim: Completing today's arts log means the award is complete.
misconceptions.correction: The log gathers evidence. The complete real portfolio needs a separate review against the award requirements.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Performers and production teams use cues, respect an audience, review real feedback and keep clear records of their own work.

lessons.artist_use_note: These are invented classroom performance examples. They are not records of real artists, an external arts visit or pupil work. Use them to compare a technique, then retain each pupil's own actual choice and view.

ta_focus.I do: Point to one clear cue or one real evidence item. Separate the teacher model from the pupil's own work.
ta_focus.We do: Ask each pupil to make or confirm a choice. If the hinge answer is uncertain, model one concrete contrast or evidence check before returning the decision.
ta_focus.Independent: Use the prompt ladder. Record actual help. Return the next choice to the pupil, and retain their own confirmed words.

lessons.evidence: Retain a dated note of each pupil's real role, choices and work or direction, actual audience when sharing occurred, real feedback if given, and support used. Keep an honest gap for anything not done. A photo or recording is optional and follows local consent procedures. A group product never replaces the individual contribution record.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Our audience is our class and invited staff only.
Choose perform, sign, speak or direct.
A quiet private share is an option.
stages.say: Today is the first slot of our final week and the performance lesson. Confirm who from the class and invited staff is actually present. There are no outside guests, families or public audience. Choose a role and audience route. Agree quiet sound, clear personal space and the open-hand stop cue.
stages.good: Each pupil confirms a role and access route. The actual allowed audience is identified without assumptions.
stages.fallback: Offer a seated silent or adult-directed share to one class member or invited staff member. A pupil may pass on the wider group share.
stages.answer: A private share within the allowed audience is valid. Record direction as direction. No share means pending; it is never recorded as a completed performance.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Find our real outline and skill plan.
Name your part and a cue.
If a plan is missing, make a short fresh one.
stages.say: Use the real outline about a smaller imagined show space: first wide moves, then a smaller space, then ideas and a small new move, then a clear end. Reuse actual pupil choices, not a claimed memory of absent sessions. If needed, make this four-part outline fresh today and agree one small role.
stages.good: Pupils know the sequence and their own contribution. Missing prior work starts fresh with today's date.
stages.fallback: Use four hand cues and let a pupil direct the adult. A two-role version can still show the change and response.
stages.answer: The response is a new safe plan after the imagined space changes. Do not physically narrow the working area or recreate distress.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Compare the two invented class examples.
Notice a start, change, response and end.
Which cue helps an audience follow?
Choose one skill to use today.
stages.say: Model one spoken and one silent version from the two fictional cards. Keep movements within a safe personal space. Show a clear pause at the choice and a final held pose. Check after the model: what evidence would show your own contribution, rather than only that the group performed?
stages.good: Adult models clear performance choices and the need for individual evidence. Pupils identify their own role, chosen cue, line, move or direction.
stages.fallback: Adult performs under a pupil's chosen cues. Ask for one point to the selected move and confirm the pupil's reason.
stages.answer: An individual role note and the pupil's own confirmed choice show contribution. A group photograph alone does not show every learner's decisions.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Agree our roles and cues.
Try one calm run.
Ask a listener to notice one skill.
Keep the story and the audience clear.
stages.say: Try a short rehearsal with performer, cue keeper and narrator or director roles. Rotate one choice so each pupil owns a contribution. Hinge: our plan names an invited staff listener, but they are absent. Can we log them as the audience? If uncertain, point to who is really here and choose a real allowed listener instead.
stages.good: The run has clear roles and a focused listener question. Audience recording matches actual presence.
stages.fallback: Use a private adult-directed trial and a listener from the class or invited staff who is present. Keep the record brief and accurate.
stages.answer: No. Record only actual listeners at the share. Choose someone present from the allowed audience, or mark the share pending and agree a next action.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Share our short performance.
Use your own role and chosen skill.
You may share privately within our class and invited staff.
Ask for one real notice.
Keep your own part in the arts log.
stages.say: Use this slot for the actual performance. Share the original smaller-show-space story in a pair, small group or private directed version. Confirm the real audience and one skill to notice. Perform or direct the four parts, then hear one actual feature-based notice if offered. Record each learner's role, choice, reason, actual audience, date and support. A learner who does not share keeps an honest pending entry with the next action; do not invent a stand-in audience or feedback.
stages.good: A real accessible performance or directed share is made to the class and invited staff only, or an honest pending record is retained. Each learner's contribution is separate from the group result.
stages.fallback: Pupil directs a seated adult to show the four-part story to one present class member or invited staff member. A silent hand cue can carry the whole role.
stages.answer: Example only: I was the cue keeper. I held the pause before our new move. One class member noticed the clear end. Record this only if those events actually occurred.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Name your actual contribution.
What did the listener really notice?
What choice would you keep?
Store your plan and feedback for Wednesday.
stages.say: Ask each maker to confirm their part, choice and any actual notice. No feedback yet is an acceptable entry. Distinguish a pupil's own view from a listener's words. Reserve the final two minutes to clear the space and keep the original plan, trials and actual share note together for Wednesday.
stages.good: The record contains real contribution and feedback or a clearly stated gap. Own view and audience response are not confused.
stages.fallback: Adult asks one prompt at a time and reads the note back. A point, sign or sketch can confirm the chosen feature.
stages.answer: I think the pause helped is the maker's view; the listener said I saw the new move is feedback. Both may be useful but should be labelled accurately.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Log what you really performed or directed.
Record the actual date and audience.
Keep your own choice and reason.
If pending, name one next action.
stages.say: Complete a real arts-log entry or confirm an adult observation. Keep the source of feedback clear. Wednesday is for reviewing the performance and closing the evidence list. A completed performance or log does not automatically complete the award.
stages.good: Dated individual entry records actual work and support, or pending evidence with a specific next action. No completion claim is made.
stages.fallback: Adult records exact confirmed words or gesture meaning. A photo or recording is not required.
stages.answer: Example only: I directed a silent point to the word Change for one invited staff listener. Next I will practise a clearer end. Use the learner's actual contribution and audience.

Supported: Pick a small role or direct an adult.
Use our four short story parts.
Share with one class member or invited staff member.
Confirm your real part and one choice.
Independent: Use the actual story outline and your role.
Share with clear cues for the allowed audience.
Ask one listener to notice a skill.
Log your part, actual audience, choice and real feedback.
Aspire: Help the group use a clear pause and end cue.
Explain how a chosen skill helps the audience.
Optional next level: check one real skill goal and keep your own view of the result.

log: Today I performed / directed / chose to pass ___.
My real contribution was ___.
My chosen skill and reason were ___.
My actual audience and date were ___.
The listener really noticed ___ / no feedback yet.
My own view of the result is ___.
Help I used was ___.
Pending item and next action: ___.
misconceptions: A planned guest is an audience member
Only record a class member or invited staff member who actually watched or listened.
The audience decides all our choices
Listen to an actual notice, then give your own reason for a kept or changed choice.
A directed share is the same as acting it
Keep the pupil's real directions; do not claim they performed an adult's moves or voice.
kit: For up to five pupils: books or arts logs, pencils, actual outlines, trials and skill goals if available.
Clear personal spaces or safe seats; smaller story spaces remain imagined.
Audience limited to the class and invited staff who are actually present.
No outside guests, public or family audience; no invitations, devices, props or costumes needed.
Retain actual share notes and any real feedback for Wednesday's closing review.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Use a calm start cue and safe wide hand poses for the first plan.
15 to 30 seconds
Show close hands. Say: Our imagined space is smaller. Pause.
30 to 45 seconds
Offer a small wave and repeat the chosen move together.
45 to 60 seconds
Hold a comfortable final pose, relax and ask the present listener about one feature.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Use your real skill goal. After the share, say what happened. Which choice helped? What would you try next? You can speak, point or draw.
stretch.evidence: Keep your own goal, real practice note, actual share and your own view. Keep feedback only if it happened.
stretch.why_optional: This extra skills and reflection record may support later work at the next level. It is optional for Explore. The full real portfolio still needs review for the award.
stretch.good: Pupil links an actual skill goal to a real contribution, gives their own view and identifies a next step without inventing a completed trial.
stretch.fallback: Use a private class or invited staff listener. Adult records confirmed choices and actual support; directed work is labelled as direction.

models: Teacher model only: I waited until all were ready, then pointed to Change. Our real listener noticed the clear new move.
Teacher model only: My share is pending because I passed. I will ask one invited staff member for a quiet chance at the next agreed lesson.
lessons.cover: This first slot is the performance lesson. Use the real four-part smaller-show-space outline or create a fresh small one today. Confirm roles and actual audience, rehearse once, then share during Create. Only class members and invited staff may watch or listen. Keep private, seated, silent and directing routes. Record actual contribution, audience and feedback; mark uncompleted sharing pending with a next action. Store evidence for Wednesday.

cold_call.foundation: What is your real part in the piece?
cold_call.middle: Which cue or skill helps the audience follow the new plan?
cold_call.higher: What evidence separates your own contribution from the group result?

lessons.title: Review the performance and close the arts log
lessons.outcome: Review the performance; complete arts log + Bronze evidence.
lessons.goal: I can review my real contribution and check my arts-log evidence.
success: I can use real evidence to review my skill.
I can check A, B, C and D and mark gaps honestly.
I can give my own view and one next action.
words: Look back at real work and choices.
Work or a clear note of what really happened.
Your own view of what you did and learned.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find the actual plan, trial and share note.
Use your own work and words.
Missing evidence stays pending.
stages.say: This second slot closes the review and arts log. Use Monday's real performance evidence where it exists. No one has to reconstruct an absent pupil's performance or invent a listener. If an item is missing, note the gap and a next action. You may work privately and plan in any language.
stages.good: Pupils gather genuine records and understand the evidence-first purpose without being ranked by attendance or confidence.
stages.fallback: Adult reads one actual record aloud. A pupil can confirm or correct by sign, point, speech or sketch.
stages.answer: Pending is an honest status. The purpose is a reliable review and next action, not a record that every box is complete.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Name one real skill or choice.
Find the item that helps show it.
Which words are your own view?
stages.say: Ask each pupil to name one role, cue, pause or move they actually performed or directed. Find a matching item where available. Label the pupil's account as their own recollection if it is not witnessed. Keep their own view separate from a listener's actual words.
stages.good: Pupil connects a real contribution to evidence and distinguishes own reflection from feedback.
stages.fallback: Offer two skill words and read a real note. Ask: is this right, or what would you change?
stages.answer: My pause helped the scene is a personal view; the listener said the end was clear is feedback only if a real listener said it. Both are labelled honestly.

stages.name: I do
pupil: See a teacher evidence review.
A real item supports a claim.
A plan is not proof it happened.
What should stay pending?
stages.say: Show clearly labelled teacher models: a plan to share, a real role note and a blank feedback line. I can say I planned the share, but without an actual share record I cannot claim an audience. Check after the model: can a teacher's good example become a pupil's missing practice note? Explain the honest next action instead.
stages.good: Adult models a claim, source and gap, and pupils reject fabricated evidence. No example is presented as a pupil record.
stages.fallback: Use two labels: real item and pending. Pupil directs the adult to place one example under each.
stages.answer: No. A teacher model is exploration, not the pupil's own practice. Record the missing item as pending and plan a real opportunity or evidence check.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Check one real item under A, B, C or D.
Say what it shows and whose work it is.
Check actual date, audience and support.
Mark a gap and next action.
stages.say: Use a genuine anonymous class item or an explicit teacher model. A is real participation; B an explored example and own view; C an idea, actual trial and change; D an actual share with date and audience. Hinge: if a group performed, can we tick every pupil's contribution from the group title alone? If uncertain, model a separate role-and-choice note for one learner and ask again.
stages.good: Pupils use the content of evidence rather than a title or group label. Individual contribution and accurate audience are checked.
stages.fallback: Read one short entry and ask for a point to what it shows. Adult scribes the pupil's actual judgement and reason.
stages.answer: No. Each learner needs a record of their own actual part. A plan or group title does not prove individual attendance, contribution, skill or feedback.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Review your real performance or direction.
Check A Take part, B Explore, C Create and D Share.
Give your own view and reason.
Mark gaps pending. Add a next action.
Optional next level: check your real skill plan, practice and learning.
stages.say: Use the final evidence list. A: actual role and support. B: actual source explored, notice and own view, with class models labelled as such. C: own idea, real trials, tested change and reason. D: actual share, real date and allowed audience, plus feedback only where given. Add a personal performance reflection supported by available items. For optional next level work, check a real skill goal or plan, actual practice, tested change, own view and reason, genuine learning reflection and next step. Record real feedback or sharing evidence where available. Keep missing items pending with the exact next action; do not fill them with a model or invented performance.
stages.good: A closing arts-log list locates real evidence and honest gaps. Each pupil gives their own supported reflection. Optional additional evidence is retained only when it exists, and no automatic award completion is claimed.
stages.fallback: Adult checks one real item at a time, using keep, pending and next action choices. Pupil confirms exact words or gesture meaning. No public sharing, new recording or written paragraph is required.
stages.answer: Example only: My role note supports A. My view of the class example supports B. The revised outline supports C. My actual share note supports D. My skill plan is present, but the second practice is pending; next I will practise the cue twice. The learner's list must match their own real items.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Read your evidence list with an adult.
Can you find each real item?
Does each gap have a next action?
Keep your own words and real records together.
stages.say: Read the record back and invite corrections. Check actual dates, audience and support, and distinguish direction from physical or vocal performance. Confirm the own-view statement belongs to the pupil. Reserve the final two minutes for calm storage. The complete portfolio still needs a separate review; the checklist does not complete the award.
stages.good: The pupil confirms the record, available items can be found, gaps have actions and no invented evidence or completion claim appears.
stages.fallback: Use one entry at a time. Let the pupil point, sign or change a word. Adult records the actual support used.
stages.answer: An honest list may have pending items in A, B, C or D and in optional next level work. Never turn a missing item into a completed claim.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: My skill changed or stayed ___ because ___.
My own view is ___.
My next action is ___.
My list keeps real work and honest gaps.
stages.say: Finish a short own reflection and one practical next step. State which evidence is ready for review and which is pending. Keep the actual work and note together. Thank pupils for their specific contribution without promising an award outcome.
stages.good: Dated personal reflection, evidence list and next action close the term's work honestly. Award completion remains a separate review.
stages.fallback: Pupil confirms one view and one action by point, sign or speech. Adult writes the confirmed words and records help.
stages.answer: Example only: I kept the pause because it helped our change stand out. My next action is to find my real trial note. Use the pupil's own view and genuine next action.

Supported: Check one real item at a time with an adult.
Point to A, B, C or D, or pending.
Say or show one real skill choice.
Confirm your own view and a next action.
Independent: Check your real A, B, C and D evidence.
Review your actual role, skill and feedback.
Give your own view with a reason.
Mark gaps pending and list exact next actions.
Aspire: Complete the same honest evidence review.
Compare two actual trials or choices.
Explain your view of what helped the audience.
Optional next level: check real skill goals, practice, learning and the next action.

A Take part: real item and location ___ / pending.
B Explore: real source, notice and own view ___ / pending.
C Create: own idea, real trial and change ___ / pending.
D Share: actual date, audience and role ___ / pending.
Real feedback ___ / no feedback yet.
My own view is ___ because ___.
My skill reflection and next step are ___.
Optional next level: real skill plan ___; practice ___; tested change ___; own view and learning ___ / pending.
Gap, missing item and exact next action: ___.
Actual support and pupil confirmation: ___.
misconceptions: The same evidence proves every part of the award
Check what each real item actually shows. The full portfolio needs a separate review.
A missed performance can be recreated in a review note
Keep it pending. A fresh later opportunity gets its own actual date and audience.
An adult should improve the learner's view
Scribe exact confirmed words. Help with access, then return the judgement and next choice to the learner.
kit: For up to five pupils: books or arts logs, pencils and each pupil's actual plan, trials, role note, share record and feedback where available.
A to D headings and the optional additional evidence checklist.
Each pupil keeps their own contribution record separate from the group outline.
No new performance audience, outside guest, device, photograph or external visit is needed.
Keep missing items pending with an exact action and the next agreed chance to do or check it.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show a labelled teacher plan to share. Say: This is a plan, not proof of an audience.
15 to 30 seconds
Show a real teacher role note. Say what the note actually supports.
30 to 45 seconds
Check A, B, C and D. Mark the missing share or feedback pending.
45 to 60 seconds
Add a next action and an own-view sentence. Keep optional skill evidence only where real.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Check your real skill plan and practice. What did you try? What changed? Give your own view and reason. Say what you learned and one next step.
stretch.evidence: Keep real plans, trials, changes and your own words. Add real feedback or sharing notes if you have them. Mark gaps pending and add the next action.
stretch.why_optional: This additional skills, own-view and learning record may support later work at the next level. It is optional for Explore. A complete real portfolio needs a separate review for the award.
stretch.good: Pupil locates actual skill planning and practice evidence, explains a tested choice in their own words, reflects on learning and records honest gaps with specific next actions.
stretch.fallback: Adult checks one item at a time and records exact confirmed choices. A pupil may point, sign, speak or draw. Directed practice is labelled as directed.

models: Teacher model only: I pointed to Change. My role note shows my direction and the listener noticed a clear end. I think the pause helped because it gave time to follow the change.
Teacher model only: My real skill plan is present. The second practice note is missing, so it is pending. Next I will check the stored log, then agree a fresh practice if needed.
lessons.cover: This is the second-slot performance review and arts-log closing lesson. Work from actual plans, trials and Monday share records. Review each learner's own part and view, then locate A to D evidence. Check optional additional skill plan, real practice, tested change and learning where available. Mark every missing item pending with an exact action. Never invent attendance, audience, feedback or a missed performance, and never declare the award complete from this checklist.

cold_call.foundation: Which real item shows your own contribution?
cold_call.middle: What does your evidence show about your skill choice?
cold_call.higher: Which parts are ready for review, and what exact action addresses each gap?

closing_evidence_list: A Take part: keep a real dated note of what you did or directed and the help you used.
B Explore: keep a real example you saw or heard, its source, what you noticed and your own view. Label an invented class model as a class model.
C Create: keep your own idea, a real trial or outline, a change you tested and your reason.
D Share: keep what you really shared, the actual date and audience, and any feedback that really happened. If no feedback was given, say so.
Optional next level: locate a real skill goal or plan, actual practice, tested change, own view and reason, learning reflection and next step. Keep genuine feedback and sharing notes where available.
For each gap, record pending, the missing item and a specific next action. Do not invent a performance, audience, feedback, attendance or completed practice.
The pupil confirms their own words and actual support. Completing this lesson or list does not automatically complete the award.

scope: Explore for both pathways. Optional GROW next level stretch retains additional evidence without changing core success criteria.
timing: Arrival 0-3; Starter 3-6; I do 6-12; We do 12-18; Create 18-32; Review 32-37; Exit 37-40 minutes.
